title: Comparison of a finite normal cover with an etale extension over a dense open
statement: Let B be a locally Noetherian integral scheme whose local rings are integrally closed [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let n:N → B and p:E → B be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with p etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose every stalk of N is an integrally closed domain. Let U be a nonempty open of B such that n^{-1}U is dense in N and n|_U is etale. Given an isomorphism e_U:N|_U ≅ E|_U over U, there is an isomorphism e:N ≅ E with e;p = n. Empty and disconnected covers are allowed. This asserts only comparison with an already supplied etale extension, not existence of that extension.

source.place: Tags 035I, 035L and 0BQM; finite normal algebra comparison in Tag 0EYJ, step 3 of lem-sbc-finite-normal-depth-two-purity

proof.text: For each point z of E, choose affine opens T around z and V around p(z), with T contained in the preimage of V. The section-ring map Gamma(B,V) to Gamma(E,T) is etale. For each prime a of Gamma(B,V), its prime localization is isomorphic to the stalk of B at the corresponding point of V, and hence is a normal domain by integrality of B and hB. Apply etale ascent of normality to the section-ring map. Its localization at the prime corresponding to z is isomorphic to E.presheaf.stalk z. Transport domainhood and integral closedness along this localization isomorphism. This is the proved private normal_stalks_of_etale helper.

The nonempty open U is dense in the irreducible space B by Mathlib IsOpen.dense. The finite etale map p is open: Mathlib supplies UniversallyOpen from flatness and local finite presentation and Scheme.Hom.isOpenMap. Apply Dense.preimage to conclude that p inverse image of U is dense in E. This is a direct application of the imported Mathlib declarations, with no auxiliary unproved statement.

Apply finite_normal_iso_of_dense_open to n and p, the supplied normal-domain stalks hN, the normal-domain stalks of E from step 1, U, hdense, the density from step 2, eU and heU. All hypotheses of the existing general comparison are supplied; no construction of relative normalization is needed here. The hypothesis hnU remains in the unchanged signature but the more general comparison does not require it.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_normal_iso_of_dense_open_etale_comparison
    {B N E : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian B] [IsIntegral B]
    (hB : ∀ y : B, IsIntegrallyClosed (B.presheaf.stalk y))
    (n : N ⟶ B) (p : E ⟶ B) [IsFinite n] [IsFinite p] [Etale p]
    (hN : ∀ z : N, IsDomain (N.presheaf.stalk z) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (N.presheaf.stalk z))
    (U : B.Opens) (hU : (U : Set B).Nonempty)
    (hdense : Dense (↑(n ⁻¹ᵁ U) : Set N))
    (hnU : Etale (n ∣_ U))
    (eU : (n ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme ≅ (p ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme)
    (heU : eU.hom ≫ p ∣_ U = n ∣_ U) :
    ∃ e : N ≅ E, e.hom ≫ p = n
